page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number at the top right. Within the column: a continued paragraph, three small titled sections (level 2 headings), and a closing division heading with a sub-title, set below a horizontal rule. Signature at the foot right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: stamentum, cum in eodem statu manente testatore, ipsius testamenti jus vitiatur. in princ.inst.cod.
main_text.head: Quot modis id accidit?
main_text.p: Tribus: Primò, si quis post factum testamentum adoptaverit sibi filium pei Imperatorem, cum, qui est sui juris: aut per praetorem secundum Imperatoris constitutionem, cum, qui in potestate parentis fuerit: testamentum ejus rumpitur, quasi agnatione sui haeredis. §.rumpitur.inst.cod.
Secundò, posteriore quoq; testamento, quod jure perfectum est, superius rumpitur. §. posteriore. instit.cod.
Tertiò, alio autem modo testamenta jure facta infirmantur: veluti cum is, qui fecit testamentum, capite deminutus sit. §. alio. inst.cod.

head.i: Infirmatur etiam testamentum, quando testator dicit se nolle superius valere?

main_text.p: Ex hoc solo non potest infirmari testamentū quod postea testator id noluerit valere: usq; adeo, ut & si quis post factum prius testamentum posterius faceie[?] coeperit. §.ex.eo.inst.cod.

head.i: Potestne quis litis causa, aut alioqui contra leges, principem instituere?

main_text.p: Non potest: licet enim (inquiunt principes) legibus soluti simus, attamen legibus vivimus. §.final, inst.cod.
main_text.head: QUIS EST DECIMUS octavus Titulus? De inofficioso testamento. Von einem unbedachtsam testament.

page.notes: Printed rule (horizontal line) between the second and third sections is not text. Page number "487" and running head "IURIS." are at the top. Doubtful readings: "pei" (in "sibi filium pei Imperatorem") printed as shown; "faceie[?]" in the paragraph beginning "Ex hoc solo" is unclear and possibly misprinted for "fecerit"; "quōd" was copied as "quod" (the mark over the o is faint). The first word of the page is a fragment ("stamentum"), the end of "testamentum" from the previous page. The black-letter opening word of the last heading reads as "Von" (printed with a Fraktur V). The division heading has no printed numeral, so no caput attribute is given. Level-2 headings are the question-titles of the sections, italic or roman as printed.
